cells.pair_definition_catalyst: Your Order is the rules you answer to and the rank you hold by them. Earth makes it steady, a rule that stays once you agree. As a catalyst, the standard comes late. You take a dare sooner than a post, and you find your pace after someone sets it.
cells.pair_advise_catalyst: You do your best work when someone else sets the deadline. Put yourself under one. Sign up for the race, the exam or the course with a date on it. Tell one person above you what you will deliver and when. Keep one standing rule at home, the same sleep hour every night. Pay one bill the day it arrives.

passages.keep_as_is: You stay calm under pressure, and it shows. Pressure hands you something solid to hold, and you save your calm for the hard moment ahead of the ordinary day.
passages.close: When a quiet day comes, give it some calm too, because that calm is yours anyway.
audit_notes: MINOR E-32: The logic is thin, and the close is advice.

passages.keep_as_is: Whenever pressure comes on, you turn calm. You spend that calm on a crisis ahead of an ordinary week, and the ordinary weeks get skipped.
passages.close: If you keep one stretch clear of crisis, you find that the calm comes with you, the rest with it.

passages.keep_as_is: Your calm is what you offer first in a crisis. You would rather carry the hard part for someone than watch them shake, and you take it off their hands before their calm gets a chance.
passages.close: Let someone else stay calm beside you for once.

passages.keep_as_is: Taking charge is a reflex for you. You would rather own a wrong call than leave one with no owner, and you take charge before anyone asks.
passages.close: If you hand a few calls to someone else, taking charge goes back to being a choice.

passages.keep_as_is: Whenever a plan stalls, you take charge, wanted or not. Deciding feels like safety to you, more than waiting ever does, and calls that were never yours end up with you.
passages.close: When you turn one down, you keep the evening it would have eaten.

passages.keep_as_is: For you, looking after a group means taking charge of it. Handing people an answer comes easier to you than waiting while they find one, and the finding is what you take from them.
passages.close: Leave one call open long enough for someone else to make.

passages.keep_as_is: Pushing through is how you get to the end of anything hard. You need something to push against, and you finish under strain more easily than at ease.
passages.close: Push on, and notice which jobs you only finish when something pushes back.

passages.keep_as_is: Under strain, you push through without a second thought. You would sooner push to the far side than ask for less, and you never try the lighter road.
passages.close: Make one job easy on purpose, and keep the strength that pushing costs.

passages.keep_as_is: Pushing through, you carry the people with you at your pace. You would rather hold the pace than slow it for someone, and that costs them the pause you never take.
passages.close: When you match the slowest once, you see what gets done anyway.
audit_notes: TWEAK E-49: "Whenever" opens two passages on one page.

cells.pair_definition_catalyst: Your Expression is the gate where inner work becomes outer fact. Earth makes it slow and solid, made to last. As a catalyst, the gate sticks, and you give quietly rather than show what you can do. You pay in kindness not given and talent not shown.
cells.pair_advise_catalyst: What you keep inside does not count as finished. Make one thing a week that someone else can hold. Say the opinion you have been sitting on to one person. Show a child or a friend something you know how to do. Write one line down before bed.

passages.keep_as_is: Proving a point matters more to you than making it. Because a finished thing argues better than you could out loud, you would rather prove an idea than pitch it.
passages.close: You pay in time, and you get to be right in a way that lasts.

passages.keep_as_is: Proving it is the only kind of winning you trust. Since you prove rather than pitch, you let the chances that needed a quick yes go by.
passages.close: You lose credit for ideas that were yours first, so pitch one before the proof is done.

passages.keep_as_is: You prove an idea before you share it. Whenever you would rather show a result than explain a plan, you keep people out of it until it is done.
passages.close: Tell one person the plan early, since a surprise is harder to help than a sketch.

passages.keep_as_is: Speaking plainly comes easier to you than softening it. Since a true thing said flat feels more honest than a kind thing dressed up, you speak plainly rather than nicely.
passages.close: You pay for it in warmth, and to you the truth is worth it.

passages.keep_as_is: Speaking plainly is how you stay honest with yourself. You would rather be understood than liked, so you say what goes unsaid and give up the easy welcome of keeping quiet.
passages.close: Soften one true thing a week, because you wanted that welcome too.

passages.keep_as_is: You speak plainly to the people who matter most to you. Where the truth counts for more than the landing, you hand it over without the cushion it needed.
passages.close: Add the cushion sometimes, because you want them to land softly too.

passages.keep_as_is: Rules read to you as first drafts. Since you would rather fix a bad rule than follow it, you rewrite it in the doing and in plain sight.
passages.close: You spend a while being marked wrong, and the rewrite tends to look like sense later.

passages.keep_as_is: Rewriting a rule is your answer to one that makes no sense. Each time you choose to fix it rather than obey it, you lose the credit that following it would earn.
passages.close: Follow one you dislike this month, because that approval was yours too.

passages.keep_as_is: You rewrite a rule that stops making sense under the people standing on it. Since you fix it ahead of keeping the peace, you change the footing with no warning.
passages.close: Give the warning first, because the rule you found pointless was somebody's floor.
audit_notes: MINOR E-21: A garden-path opener. Keep the excellent "somebody's floor".

cells.pair_definition_catalyst: Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Earth makes it steady, so what you learn sinks in. As a catalyst, nothing settles for long, and you work it out alone rather than lean on anyone. You judge best once you give a question its night.
cells.pair_advise_catalyst: Your judgment is only as good as the time you let it take. Read one book slowly instead of five fast. Ask the oldest person you trust how they would do it, and hear them out to the end. Keep one evening a week with nobody in it. Sleep on anything that costs money.

passages.keep_as_is: Teaching yourself matters more to you than being taught. Needing to understand before you trust, you teach yourself from odd sources rather than take the standard lesson.
passages.close: Let someone teach you from time to time, since a lesson only you know is lonely.

passages.keep_as_is: Whenever you want to know something, you teach it to yourself instead of asking. Teaching yourself an answer costs you a month where being taught it costs an hour.
passages.close: Ask for the hour sometimes, because you pay for each self-taught month in rest.

passages.keep_as_is: Rarely do you pass on the lesson you taught yourself. You taught it by a route too odd to explain, so you keep the knowing rather than tell it.
passages.close: Hand someone the messy version, because you leave anyone learning from you without the self-taught part.

passages.keep_as_is: You read between the lines before you finish the lines. Needing to know a thing from underneath, you trust what sits between the words over what they say.
passages.close: Wait for the reason to catch up, since you cannot pass a hunch on without proof.

passages.keep_as_is: Between the lines is where you are quickest and hardest to follow. You go with the read rather than wait for proof, so the doubt stays yours.
passages.close: Write the read down, since you pay for every unchecked read in doubt about your own mind.
audit_notes: MINOR E-26: The doubt is said twice, and writing a read down does not check it.

passages.keep_as_is: Whatever gets left between the lines, you read first and skip asking. Since your read lands before your question, you answer what sits under the words instead of the words.
passages.close: Ask the plain question, because you take from people the chance to say it themselves.

passages.keep_as_is: Thinking alone is how you do your best thinking. Because you need the whole picture before you share any of it, you want the quiet ahead of the company.
passages.close: Take one invitation you usually turn down, since you give up company for thinking alone.

passages.keep_as_is: After a day of company, you need an hour of thinking alone to feel yourself. You think alone to fill up rather than hide, so you guard it over sleep.
passages.close: Guard the sleep too, since you take those hours from a night your body needed.

passages.keep_as_is: Your best thinking happens alone, and you go off to it without saying how long. Thinking best out of reach, you let the solo hours run long rather than stop early.
passages.close: Name the length first, since you give those waiting no time to expect you.
audit_notes: MINOR E-25: "best thinking" then "Thinking best" says it twice, and "long" appears 3 times. The close is garbled.

cells.pair_definition_catalyst: Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Earth makes it steady, so what you claim lasts. As a catalyst, the wanting outruns the keeping, and you chase the next venture instead of holding what you have. You end up owning far less than you built.
cells.pair_advise_catalyst: You want things far more easily than you claim them. Put one goal in writing with a date beside it. Move a fixed sum into savings on the same day each month. Tell the person you love one plan for the year and keep to it. Finish the small thing before you start another.

passages.keep_as_is: You see a chance long before anyone else wants it. Having somewhere next to go is your safety, so you watch where a thing is heading more than what it is.
passages.close: Looking far costs you some of what is near, and the trade favours you.
audit_notes: TWEAK E-39: US spelling; the other energy pages use "favour/favours".

passages.keep_as_is: Looking far comes naturally, and it pays. The next place is clearer to you than this one, so you see the far chance sooner than the near one.
passages.close: You lose the opening at hand most, and one quick look before passing it keeps it.

passages.keep_as_is: You look past the people closest to you toward the next place. Seeing far is how you keep them safe, and that gives the plan more of you than them.
passages.close: If you let them look with you, you see far enough for all of them.

passages.keep_as_is: A chance within reach is hard to leave alone, because standing in place feels like losing. You take the one that is here rather than wait for a safer one.
passages.close: You take them best with your eyes open, since some of them cost you.

passages.keep_as_is: Taking the chance pays you more than waiting does. Moving makes you feel alive, so you put money into what moves rather than what is safe.
passages.close: Take the next one with money you can spare, because the wrong ones cost what the sure ones kept.
audit_notes: MINOR E-14: The close does not parse on first read, and it is advice (E-02).

passages.keep_as_is: You take the chance for everyone whose money sits beside yours. Moving feels safer to you than staying, and you put their calm into the venture with your own.
passages.close: You take it for them too, and choosing its size with them costs you nothing.

passages.keep_as_is: A win only feels real to you once you have shared it. Providing is where you feel most yourself, and you share a good month rather than put it away.
passages.close: You share because it is right for you, and the thinner cushion is the price.

passages.keep_as_is: Sharing the win is your natural generosity, and it leaves you short. What you give in a good year you lack in a lean one, because giving comes ahead of keeping.
passages.close: If you keep some of each win back, the lean year stops costing you.

passages.keep_as_is: You share each win rather than sit on it. Giving in bursts is your way of loving, and you hand them plenty one year and nothing the next.
passages.close: You do them more good sharing in a shape that lasts, since they come back.
audit_notes: MINOR E-15: "since they come back" has no clear sense.

cells.pair_definition_catalyst: Your Body is the strength the whole of you stands on. Earth gives it weight and patience under a load. As a catalyst, you bend sooner and lean on a peer's view or step back from a stake you share. You end up living by calls that were not yours.
cells.pair_advise_catalyst: Most of what you give up, you give up tired. Wait for the whole answer before you agree to anything. Ask one peer to hold the line with you for a week. Keep one routine that survives a bad month. Say yes sitting down.

passages.keep_as_is: You are better with a rival in sight. Your own pace never quite wakes you, so you measure yourself against a person rather than a plan.
passages.close: Pick your rivals on purpose, and you turn a reflex into the fastest way you grow.

passages.keep_as_is: Being better with rivals leaves you rarely at your best alone. Without someone to beat, you drift rather than push, so the goals only you care about wait longest.
passages.close: Find a rival for the private goals too, and you stop leaving your own for last.

passages.keep_as_is: Better with a rival, you turn a peer into one without asking. You would rather race someone than keep them company, and you hand a contest to a friend who wanted none.
passages.close: Name the race, and you give them the choice to run it.

passages.keep_as_is: You bet big because only a real stake gets all of you, and you would rather risk a lot on one move than a little on many.
passages.close: If you let small bets count too, you stop missing the gains that come slowly.

passages.keep_as_is: Where you bet big, you lose at the same size. You stake the whole amount instead of keeping some in reserve.
passages.close: When you hold back one part of each bet, you keep the savings a single loss would take.

passages.keep_as_is: On a shared stake, you bet someone else's year with your own. You would rather win it all for both of you than keep half safe, and their caution becomes your dare.
passages.close: Ask first, because you keep a partner who chose the risk.

passages.keep_as_is: With a win in hand, you would rather share the credit than keep it, because a prize means more with your people inside it.
passages.close: When a win can count before you have shared it, you get to enjoy it twice.

passages.keep_as_is: Taking the credit alone feels like showing off to you. You hand out credit rather than keep it, and your own work goes unnamed.
passages.close: If you put your own name on your part, you stop losing the chances that follow credit.

passages.keep_as_is: The credit you share lands on people who did not run for it. You would rather have company at the finish than stand there alone, and you pass out what only you earned.
passages.close: Name who did what, to give praise each person can use.

cells.pair_definition_catalyst: Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Earth makes it steady, so what you learn sinks in. As a catalyst, nothing settles for long, and you work it out alone rather than lean on anyone. You judge best once you give a question its night.
cells.pair_advise_catalyst: Your judgment is only as good as the time you let it take. Read one book slowly instead of five fast. Ask the oldest person you trust how they would do it, and hear them out to the end. Keep one evening a week with nobody in it. Sleep on anything that costs money.

passages.keep_as_is: Your presence calms people before your words do. Since you need people safe rather than impressed, you calm them with the slow question ahead of the fix.
passages.close: Let someone be the calm one for you sometimes, because you need calming as much as anyone.

passages.keep_as_is: Being the calm one comes naturally, and you forget it weighs anything. You calm someone through a bad month rather than admit your own, so you put yourself last.
passages.close: Say the tired thing out loud, since you pay for everyone's calm in rest not taken.

passages.keep_as_is: Whenever you watch someone close to you come apart, you become the calm under them. You calm them rather than get calmed, and hide every shake of your own.
passages.close: Let them see you wobble, because you give them no chance to calm you back.

passages.keep_as_is: Knowing what works comes easier to you than hoping something unproven will. Because you need an answer to have lasted, you reach for what has worked over what sounds clever.
passages.close: Give a new idea one honest try, since every answer you trust was new once.

passages.keep_as_is: Faced with a new way, you wait for proof rather than try it. Knowing what works means more to you than being early, so you land safe and late.
passages.close: Try one untested thing, because you miss the chances that wanted you early.

passages.keep_as_is: The advice you give has already worked somewhere. Knowing what works better than what someone hopes for, you send their new idea home with an old one.
passages.close: Hear the new idea out, since you take from them the chance to be wrong their own way.

passages.keep_as_is: You teach a thing a third time with the patience of the first. Needing the person to get there, you teach at their pace ahead of your own.
passages.close: Keep one hour a week that teaches nobody, because only you fill your patience back up.

passages.keep_as_is: Teaching someone patiently is easy for you and hard to count. Since you wait for them rather than hurry them, you hand your own evening to the teaching.
passages.close: Say no to one lesson a week, because you take every patient lesson out of your rest.

passages.keep_as_is: Your patience is what you teach with first. You teach it a second time instead of watching someone struggle, and take the struggle that made it theirs.
passages.close: Let them not know a while longer, since you take the practice with every answer handed over.
audit_notes: MINOR E-27: "it" has no clear referent, "take" appears 3 times, and "Let them not know" is awkward.

cells.pair_definition_catalyst: Your Order is the rules you answer to and the rank you hold by them. Earth makes it steady, a rule that stays once you agree. As a catalyst, the standard comes late. You take a dare sooner than a post, and you find your pace after someone sets it.
cells.pair_advise_catalyst: You do your best work when someone else sets the deadline. Put yourself under one. Sign up for the race, the exam or the course with a date on it. Tell one person above you what you will deliver and when. Keep one standing rule at home, the same sleep hour every night. Pay one bill the day it arrives.

passages.keep_as_is: You keep every promise, including the ones that stopped making sense. Your word is what you stand on, and keeping it matters more to you than whether the promise fits your life now.
passages.close: If you change one promise out loud, you keep the rest whole.

passages.keep_as_is: Whenever you give your word, you keep the promise in full. You wear reliable better than happy, and the agreements that cost more each year stay put.
passages.close: When you change one out loud, you get the plan you gave up for it back.

passages.keep_as_is: Long after you stopped wanting to, you keep promises to people. Holding counts for more with you than honesty about changing, and you never tell the person that the promise went stale.
passages.close: Give one person the real answer, and let them choose.
audit_notes: MINOR E-30: "never tell" implies concealment, which is the bad-faith charge BIZ_04 names. The close is an imperative.

passages.keep_as_is: You play fair even when it costs you the win. You only trust a rule that applies to everyone, and you keep yourself to it rather than make yourself the exception.
passages.close: If you let one person see the fairness, you lose nothing.
audit_notes: MINOR E-31: The close says nothing the reader can check.

passages.keep_as_is: Where a shortcut gets you ahead, you play fair and arrive late. Being right with yourself comes ahead of arriving first, and the quick wins go to people who care less.
passages.close: Claim what you earned fairly, because the title you wait on goes elsewhere.

passages.keep_as_is: With the people closest to you, you play fair exactly as with strangers. Being fair to everyone comes ahead of being on anyone's side, and you never pick theirs either.
passages.close: Make one small exception, and see how little fairness it costs.

passages.keep_as_is: You set the standard before anyone asks for one. You would rather set a clear standard than argue over one, and the one you set binds you first.
passages.close: When you set one with people instead of for them, you share its weight.

passages.keep_as_is: Wherever a standard is missing, you set one and live under it. You take your own bar as the measure ahead of anyone else's, and yours sits a step above you.
passages.close: If you set the bar where you stand, you pass it for once.

passages.keep_as_is: You set a standard for the whole group. You hold people to a standard they can see rather than guess at, and the standard you set is theirs to meet too.
passages.close: If you ask them where to set it, you find it met more gladly.
audit_notes: MINOR E-29: Sentence 2 is circular: a standard set for a group is theirs to meet by definition. The close is advice (E-02).

cells.pair_definition_catalyst: Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Earth makes it steady, so what you claim lasts. As a catalyst, the wanting outruns the keeping, and you chase the next venture instead of holding what you have. You end up owning far less than you built.
cells.pair_advise_catalyst: You want things far more easily than you claim them. Put one goal in writing with a date beside it. Move a fixed sum into savings on the same day each month. Tell the person you love one plan for the year and keep to it. Finish the small thing before you start another.

passages.keep_as_is: Making a thing last is a craft you practice without noticing. Waste feels to you like a small loss of control, so you repair what you own rather than replace it.
passages.close: You pay by living with the older version a while longer than you need.

passages.keep_as_is: Making things last keeps you in control of what you own. You put hours into repairs ahead of the better thing on offer, because replacing feels like waste.
passages.close: Once fixing costs more than the thing is worth, letting it go gives you those hours back.

passages.keep_as_is: You keep old things going for everyone around you. Fixing beats choosing for you, and you have the people at home living with your kept things rather than their own.
passages.close: You make the rest last, and one new thing a year is theirs to pick.

passages.keep_as_is: Saving comes first for you, ahead of the treat and the trip. A cushion is what lets you relax, and you put money away rather than enjoy it.
passages.close: Saving first suits you, and a few good things you were slow to buy are the price.

passages.keep_as_is: Saving first is the quiet skill under everything you own. You would rather be covered than pleased, and the good thing you can afford keeps waiting.
passages.close: If you spend one saved sum on something you want, the pleasure you put off stops being the price.
audit_notes: MINOR E-16: The sentence has to be read twice.

passages.keep_as_is: You save for the people you love ahead of spending on them. A safe future is the gift you trust, and you give them the cushion rather than the dinner.
passages.close: Spend part of it on them this year, because it was for them all along.

passages.keep_as_is: Being loyal costs you less than leaving ever would. The known thing keeps you safe, and you hold what is already yours instead of looking elsewhere.
passages.close: You stay a while past where it serves you, and that is the price of loyalty like yours.

passages.keep_as_is: Your loyalty stays put, and it pays in people who stay. You keep choosing what is yours rather than ask if it chooses you too.
passages.close: Asking every so often costs you little, while loyalty to what does not love you back costs you closeness.

passages.keep_as_is: Loyalty is how you love, shown by staying. You keep the one you have rather than look around, and you let the staying speak for you.
passages.close: Being chosen again is a thing you give out loud, and you give it less than you mean to.
audit_notes: MINOR E-12: Being chosen is something you receive, not something you give, so the close is illogical.

cells.pair_definition_catalyst: Your Body is the strength the whole of you stands on. Earth gives it weight and patience under a load. As a catalyst, you bend sooner and lean on a peer's view or step back from a stake you share. You end up living by calls that were not yours.
cells.pair_advise_catalyst: Most of what you give up, you give up tired. Wait for the whole answer before you agree to anything. Ask one peer to hold the line with you for a week. Keep one routine that survives a bad month. Say yes sitting down.

passages.keep_as_is: On your own terms, you set a bar and trust it more than any outside grade. Each time you clear it, you set it a little higher.
passages.close: If you leave it in place for a week, you get the satisfaction you keep putting off.

passages.keep_as_is: Where you set your own bar, you set it alone. Since no one else's standard moves you, you stay steady while you skip the help a peer would give.
passages.close: Let a peer check the bar sometimes, and you win back the help you walk past.

passages.keep_as_is: The bar you set for yourself travels to everyone beside you. Because you never say it, you expect a match rather than ask for one.
passages.close: Say the bar out loud once, and you give the people beside you a fair chance to meet it.

passages.keep_as_is: You need no backup, and owing no one is how you feel safe. You trust yourself as backup more than anyone you could call.
passages.close: Go without backup only where it counts, because you need your strength for those days.

passages.keep_as_is: Without backup you never learn what being covered feels like. You give that relief far more than you accept it, since accepting would mean admitting a need.
passages.close: When you let yourself need backup, you get back the rest you have been doing without.

passages.keep_as_is: Standing without backup keeps the people who would stand behind you at a distance. You would rather owe nothing than let a friend in, and that leaves them nothing to hold.
passages.close: Call on a friend as backup once, to show them they count.

passages.keep_as_is: Whatever the week brings, you hold steady. Calm is what you trust, and you hold steady instead of riding every mood around you.
passages.close: Whenever you hold steady by choice, not from habit, you keep some of that calm for yourself.

passages.keep_as_is: Holding steady for everyone, you hide your worst days. You absorb a bad day instead of naming it, and it settles in your body as tiredness.
passages.close: Tell one friend about a rough week, to take in some of the comfort you give everyone else.

passages.keep_as_is: Good news or bad, you hold steady and look the same. You would sooner keep a level face than show a peer what you feel.
passages.close: When you let one peer see what moves you, you stop leaving them to guess what matters.

cells.pair_definition_catalyst: Your Expression is the gate where inner work becomes outer fact. Earth makes it slow and solid, made to last. As a catalyst, the gate sticks, and you give quietly rather than show what you can do. You pay in kindness not given and talent not shown.
cells.pair_advise_catalyst: What you keep inside does not count as finished. Make one thing a week that someone else can hold. Say the opinion you have been sitting on to one person. Show a child or a friend something you know how to do. Write one line down before bed.

passages.keep_as_is: Giving comes to you before the question does. Being useful is how you feel you belong, so you give first rather than wait to be asked.
passages.close: You lose nothing by waiting for the question, since a gift asked for is the one that gets kept.

passages.keep_as_is: Before the asking, you have usually already given. Because the gift comes ahead of the need, you never learn whether you were wanted or only useful.
passages.close: You pay in a closeness you never get to test until you let the asking come first.

passages.keep_as_is: Giving first is your way of saying you noticed. Each time you give instead of waiting to be needed, you take from the people closest to you the small pride of asking.
passages.close: Leave them the asking along with the giving.

passages.keep_as_is: What you make is made to last, slowly and on purpose. The making itself is the enjoyment, so you make things for the years rather than for the showing.
passages.close: You deserve the showing as much as the making, because work that stays unseen stays unused.

passages.keep_as_is: Making things last is your idea of doing something right. Since the work is only right once it holds, you would rather be finished than first.
passages.close: Show one thing before it is done, or the chances that wanted you early close while you keep making.
audit_notes: MINOR E-37: Two gods share one figure (the image BIZ_04 already moved away from: "chances that wanted a yes").

passages.keep_as_is: You make things last for your family rather than arrive on time. You never count the waiting, and next year you deliver what was needed this year.
passages.close: You are free to hand over an early version, and a thing used now beats one admired later.

passages.keep_as_is: Enough is a place you can live in. Being happy with what is here comes easier than wanting, so you enjoy what you have rather than chase what you lack.
passages.close: Let yourself want more sometimes, because enough has a way of shrinking.

passages.keep_as_is: Being happy with enough spares you a lot of chasing. Because contentment feels like wisdom, you settle for what is here instead of asking for more.
passages.close: Ask for more once a year, since the chance you never test closes as quietly as you settled.

passages.keep_as_is: At home, enough is the mood you set. Whenever enough comes early for you, you settle for the people in your care rather than push for them.
passages.close: Want more out loud for them, and the size of your enough becomes the size of their life.
audit_notes: MINOR E-13: The logic is inverted: as written, wanting more makes your enough the size of their life, which is the outcome the line warns against.
